title: Faint Signal — Contingency Notes (personal scratchpad)
content:
Context:
This is my quick, no-frills scratchpad for "faint signal" behavior — intermittent token errors, sporadic small-latency spikes that don’t look like full outages, or single-region transient degrads. NOT an official runbook; meant for quick handoff during the late shift.

Definition (how I use the term):
- faint signal = low-volume, reproducible anomalies that affect a subset of requests (e.g., 0.5–3% error at the API edge) OR occasional 50–200ms tail latency blips on generation endpoints.
- Distinguish from full outage by: ability to complete requests, no circuit-breaker trips across the fleet, and lack of downstream overload metrics.

Immediate triage (10–15m):
1) Check global health pages (Console > Service Status) for obvious alerts.
2) Run quick user-facing check: curl the hosted inference health + a small generation: 
   - curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TEST_KEY" -d '{"prompt":"ping","max_tokens":4}'
   - If returns 200 with tokens -> proceed with deeper check; if 5xx, escalate.
3) Timebox logs: check last 30m for "faint"/"kvcache miss"/"rate limit" in runtime logs.
   - kubectl -n inference logs -l app=runtime --since=30m | rg "(KV_CACHE|kvcache|prefix|faint|rate limit|503)"
4) Look at SLI dashboard: per-region error %, 95/99 latency, and prefix cache hit rate.

Quick checks (order matters):
- Edge / Frontend: Confirm edge LB (nginx/fastly) 4xx/5xx counts and recent config deploys (ops-deploy channel).
- Model variant routing: Did a rollout happen? Console -> Rollouts -> recent changes.
- KV cache pressure: if prefix cache hit rate drops suddenly, expect token cost spikes and latency jitter.
- Autoscale events: Was there an infra scale up/down during window? Check infra autoscaling logs.

Fast mitigation (if user impact is real):
- Short-term: shift traffic away from suspect region via routing override (Console -> Traffic -> Region override -> divert 20% to fallback region).
- If small cohort failing due to model variant: pin route to last stable model for that API key (can do per-route pin in Console).
- Increase concurrency cap for dedicated fleet for 15 minutes (if autoscaler is slow).

Rollback recipe (model/route):
1) Identify route id from request metadata (trace id or route in Console).
2) In Console -> Routes, select route -> Rollout history -> Revert to previous stable model ID.
3) If rollbacks fail or take >10m, create a temporary route that maps the endpoint to a stable variant and do a gradual traffic cutover (20% -> 50% -> 100%).

Commands I use frequently (copy-paste):
- Check pods and restarts: kubectl get pods -n inference -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,RESTARTS:.status.containerStatuses[*].restartCount --sort-by=.status.startTime
- Quick tail for runtime errors: kubectl logs -n inference -l app=runtime -c runtime -f --since=10m | rg "error|panic|timeout|kvcache"
- Health probe to model server: curl -sS http://model-runtime-internal:8080/health | jq .

Observability pointers: where I check things
- Datadog: "redwood.*.latency" and "redwood.*.errors" dashboards (save a bookmark called "faint-signal-quick").
- Traces: Sampling window 5m, look for async tasks that balloon (queue length metric).
- Logs: prefer runtime container then gateway then infra-autoscaler logs.

Known flaky endpoints / memory hotspots (recent notes):
- token-service-eu: high 95 latency when prefix cache hit < 70%. Suspect stale KV shard.
- embedder-shard-3: occasional GC pauses causing 100–200ms tail blips (GC tuning ticket: OPS-1123).

Temporary degradation plan (when rollback/migration not possible quickly):
- Enable shorter streaming chunking on error-prone routes (reduces memory pressure).
- Apply 10s client-side timeout / fallback to degraded text-only path (documented as route override).
- If cost matters, briefly reduce sampling logging rate to 10% (annotate in incident notes).

Escalation matrix (who to ping first):
- Pager: eng-sre oncall (use #eng-sre on Slack) -> if pager triggers, call SRE lead.
- If model-specific: @LucaMartins (model runtime), @Samira (infra).
- Exec-level: only if >10% traffic affected for >30m or major revenue API keys impacted.

Handoff checklist (what I leave for next person):
- One-line summary of symptom + time window + quick mitigations attempted.
- Links: alert ID, sample trace ids, route ids, model ids used in test.
- TODOs assigned (if any) and why we didn’t fully remediate.

Example quick summary (copy template):
- Symptom: intermittent 1.8% 500s on /v1/generate in eu-west-1 between 23:12–23:40 UTC.
- Actions: diverted 25% traffic to eu-central at 23:25; rolled model route to stable at 23:33; errors dropped to 0.2%.
- Outstanding: follow-up ticket to investigate KV shard evictions (OPS-1123).

Open questions / TODO (personal):
- Add a small synthetic probe that exercises kvcache pressure scenarios nightly -> reduce detection latency.
- Add a Console quick-toggle for temporary region diversion (UX ticket).

Notes to self (micro):
- When searching logs, try regex: "(KV_CACHE|kvcache|prefix-cache|cache miss|lease expired)".
- If seeing sudden spikes in 429s, check per-key quotas before blaming runtime.
- Don’t forget to annotate the incident channel with timeframe and rollback id for auditing.

End-of-shift handoff snippet (paste into Slack):
"Quick handoff: saw faint 1–2% 500s on eu-west; diverted 25% at 23:25, rolled to stable model at 23:33; suspect kvcache shard eviction. Follow-up: OPS-1123. Leaving monitoring on; if errors >1% re-escalate. — Nadia"

Random micro-thoughts (scratch):
- Could a very low-rate bot cause prefix cache churn? log source_ip and user_agent for anomalies.
- Consider short-lived in-memory prefix cache on edge nodes for very hot prefixes.

-- end scratchpad --
simple_summary: Personal scratchpad for intermittent (low-volume) production anomalies: definitions, triage steps, quick commands, mitigations, and handoff template. Draft for oncall use.
